pinned_rule_caliber.distance_determination: SHORTEST PATH = torus Manhattan distance. Verified from the game code (fastsim.py): movement is 4-directional with per-coordinate wraparound (_MOVE_OFFSETS/_move_nbr), applied unconditionally in step phase 1; trees/bases/units never block the move itself (collisions are dynamic and resolve in phase 2). The board has NO static obstacles, so the shortest path under the movement rules equals the torus Manhattan distance = cnet2_feat.DIST, which the rule module reads directly (no re-derived metric). Destinations from cnet2_feat.DEST.
pinned_rule_caliber.form: exit overlay only; candidate generation and the comparator do not carry the rule; deterministic pure function of (obs, acts) -- the module-level LAST dict is a diagnostic side channel, overwritten per call, never read by the rule
pinned_rule_caliber.return_step: a move whose destination is at distance exactly d-1; first by the pinned direction order; if none, wait (NONE)
pinned_rule_caliber.trigger: own worker with cargo > 0 AND moves_available <= d + 2 (HOME_BUFFER=2); no min_cargo, no spare scaling, no deadliness check, no policy-probability scan
